annotationRationale: The method counts restricted permutations by dividing Alice's positions into disjoint cases, multiplying the choices within each case, and adding the case totals.
sourceMethod: Followed the second official solution, classifying Alice's chair as an end, next to an end, or the middle. Explained why the remaining choices satisfy every restriction and count each seating once.

review.mathCheck: Alice at an end gives 2×2×2×2=16 arrangements; in chair 2 or 4 gives 2×2×2=8; in chair 3 gives 2×2=4. Each case enforces both adjacency restrictions, and the cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Total: 28, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the second official approach to numbered solution 14 on page 6. The candidate also explains why both remaining orders in the end-chair case are valid.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_h232 captures addition across cases and multiplication within cases. cnm_h235 appropriately captures ordered arrangements; no permutation formula or inclusion-exclusion node is required.
